title: Enhancing Visual Paralinguistics: Motion-Guided Spatial Denoising for Non-Verbal Interaction Analysis
abstract: In Human-Computer Interaction, non-verbal cues like micro-gestures are essential for understanding human intent alongside speech. However, extracting these subtle movements in unconstrained environments is difficult due to severe visual clutter and spatial ambiguity. We propose a signal processing-inspired framework centered on a Motion-Guided Spatial Refinement Module (MG-SRM). Rather than relying solely on heavy spatial encoders, MG-SRM utilizes multi-order temporal differences to explicitly filter out static background artifacts in pose heatmaps. In addition, we introduce a Class-Learnable Fusion (CLF) strategy that adapts modality weights based on action semantics, prioritizing input streams according to the target micro-gesture. Experiments on the challenging MA-52 dataset show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance by directly improving the signal-to-noise ratio of micro-movements. Our proposed framework is highly accurate and computationally efficient, providing a robust visual frontend for multimodal conversational systems.
relevance_note: Visual micro-gesture analysis for non-verbal interaction; no speech synthesis.
